subject: The journey from kitchen survey to fitting
hook: The order a kitchen goes in, and why it matters
ig:
The order a kitchen goes in, and why it matters.

Here's a typical fitting sequence, shown as an example rather than a specific job.

The room comes first: old kitchen out, services capped or moved by the right trades, walls and floor ready.

Then everything is set from a level line. Base units are levelled on their legs so the worktop sits flat, even on a sloping floor. Tall and wall units follow and are checked against the base run.

Worktops and integrated appliances go in next. Doors, scribed fillers, end panels and plinths come last, because they're what you see and they need everything behind them to be right.

Finally, every door and drawer is adjusted so the gaps line up.

Swipe through the six stages. Planning a kitchen this year? Share this with whoever's doing it with you.

on_asset: F1: Room ready — Old kitchen out, services capped or moved by the relevant trades, walls and floor prepared. | F2: Base units set and levelled — Everything starts from a level line, so worktops sit flat even if the floor slopes. | F3: Tall and wall units — Tall housings and wall cupboards fixed securely, checked against the base run. | F4: Worktops and appliances — Worktops fitted or templated, depending on the material, and integrated appliances placed in their housings. | F5: Doors, fillers and plinths — Fillers scribed to walls, doors hung, plinths and end panels fitted. | F6: Adjust and hand over — Every door and drawer aligned, soft-close checked and the kitchen handed over clean.
